### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/service-messaging`, touching **18** documentable anchor(s).

**7** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via approvals.getRequest (sdk, the route ledger binds it to GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id, selected by route anchor /approvals/requests/:id), getRequest (sdk, the bare tail of client method approvals.getRequest, bound to GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id))_
- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via /approvals/requests/:id (route, bridged from symbol requestInfo — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol sendBack — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/automation/approvals.mdx`  _(via getRequest (sdk, the bare tail of client method approvals.getRequest, bound to GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id), /approvals/requests/:id (route, bridged from symbol requestInfo — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol sendBack — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via /approvals/requests/:id (route, bridged from symbol requestInfo — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol sendBack — its route source's handler names it))_

- `content/docs/kernel/services-checklist.mdx`  _(via /approvals/requests/:id (route, bridged from symbol requestInfo — its route source's handler names it; bridged from symbol sendBack — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via getRequest (sdk, the bare tail of client method approvals.getRequest, bound to GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via sys_notification (symbol, a field of const object PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY), getRequest (sdk, the bare tail of client method approvals.getRequest, bound to GET /api/v1/approvals/requests/:id))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-2.mdx`  _(via MessagingService (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-5.mdx`  _(via sys_notification (symbol, a field of const object PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 430e5f5ad128792a5f0e4acfbbd14ab79cd317e8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `126f017fe019eb7feff9ea9eb1e02c981307a721` — the merge of head `238d07b36509b71682396b2fcc0451d6206899c9` into base `430e5f5ad128792a5f0e4acfbbd14ab79cd317e8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 126f017fe019eb7feff9ea9eb1e02c981307a721 && git checkout 126f017fe019eb7feff9ea9eb1e02c981307a721
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 430e5f5ad128792a5f0e4acfbbd14ab79cd317e8 238d07b36509b71682396b2fcc0451d6206899c9 && git checkout -B drift-repro 430e5f5ad128792a5f0e4acfbbd14ab79cd317e8 && git merge --no-ff 238d07b36509b71682396b2fcc0451d6206899c9

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 430e5f5ad128792a5f0e4acfbbd14ab79cd317e8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 430e5f5ad128792a5f0e4acfbbd14ab79cd317e8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b389aa57dd94d069645d728f9440f0b47819fe6a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #23284 (body and every comment: the triage ruling 6148637195, the claim 6154283897, the os-dev-report 6155779257, the claim amendment 6155816752); PR #23340 (body, file list, the net diff of the head against its merge base `cc14657ede` with `main` at `614fdec832`); the check-runs on the head sha, read through the API after every run completed. Nothing built, run or re-run locally; the one log read is the red job's own, through the API.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `@objectstack/objectql` — `PLATFORM_OBJECT_TENANCY` (exported from the package index) gains `sys_notification: tenant-scoped`. Accept-set change on a system-context `insert('sys_notification', …)` that names no organization on the context or the row: `single` with exactly one organization DERIVES it; `single` with two or more, `isolated`, `group`, and `single` with zero organizations where `sys_organization` is registered REFUSE with `ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED` (500) and write nothing; the engine's `isSystem` tenant-audit auto-mute no longer covers the object. **Right.** The ledger's own admission bar is a citable writer fact: the entry cites the maintainer's ruling that names the table verbatim — 「11303 sys_inbox_message/sys_notification/sys_email 应该写 organization_id。」, already quoted on `main` in `notify-node.ts` — plus the writers this diff makes stamp the column, the same shape as the `sys_file` and `sys_approval_request` entries beside it; ADR-0131 D9 is the rule it reaches. The pinned list grows by exactly one name and every arm is pinned in `tenancy-by-object-classification.test.ts`. `ScheduleTrigger`'s BIND line on `main` already tells the operator that under `single` holding several organizations an undeclared flow's notification "will be REFUSED at the write"; this diff makes the event row do what that line says. Note: the zero-organization `single` arm is inside the narrowing, and the changeset's "Refused now" names only the walled and the several-organizations cases; its general sentence ("where no organization is derivable") covers it.

2. `@objectstack/service-messaging` — `MessagingService.emit()` (public): (a) an emit that names no organization and whose event write the engine refuses now REJECTS with the engine's envelope (`code` plus `status`) and writes nothing, where `main` stored the event row with NULL and went on; (b) when the producer passed none and the stored event row carries an organization, that organization is stamped on the outbox delivery row, the inline inbox row and the receipt (`owned`), and is what `Notification.organizationId` hands every channel. **Right** — the narrowing is the card's "no notification row is organization-less", pinned on a real `ObjectQL` over better-sqlite3 for the inline and the outbox path, the two-organization refusal included. `writeEvent` (private) now returns `{ id, organizationId? }` — internal. Observation, unchanged from `main` and outside the ask: audience resolution (`resolver.resolve`), the preference filter and the channel-availability consult still read the producer's absent `organizationId`, not the derived one (the consult runs before the write and cannot; the other two could). Not a finding against this head.

3. `@objectstack/service-automation` — the `notify` executor: a run whose context carries no `tenantId` now issues ONE `findOne` by id under `{ context: { isSystem: true } }` projecting `['id', wallColumn]`, first for the declared click-through record (`sourceObject` + `sourceId`), else the run's trigger record (`context.object` + `context.record.id`), through `createRecordWallOrganizationResolver` (`@objectstack/metadata-core`, already a dependency; the wall column, ADR-0066 opt-out honoured); an unknown object, a missing row and an empty column each fall through, a thrown read fails the step, and a run carrying `tenantId` emits the byte-identical input and reads nothing (PIN I). The `[notify] no organization in scope` WARN is gone with the NULL row it predicted. The step's failure text becomes `notify failed: CODE: message` for any thrown error carrying a string `code`, not only the refusal; `NodeExecutionResult.code` stays unset, reason in-code. **Right** — the triage direction is "the organization of the record it is about, the same anchor the inventory uses, never a guessed or default organization", and no limb here guesses. Pinned (PIN C–I) with the real engine and the real messaging service over a capturing data engine.

4. `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` — `ApprovalService.notify` (private) takes a REQUIRED `organizationId: string | null | undefined`; all 13 `this.notify({` sites at head pass `requestOrg` (while the request opens) or the stored row's `raw.organization_id`; null and empty normalise to an absent key, so the engine rule decides. Every approval notification now carries its request's organization, the user-driven `approval.requested` included. **Right** — the triage direction verbatim; the body battery opens its deals in two organizations and pins every emit's `organizationId` to the stored request row's. 12 of the 13 sites are driven (the second `approval.reminder` branch, for literal audience entries, is not); it passes the same `raw.organization_id` as its sibling, read off the diff. `ApprovalMessagingSurface.emit`'s input gains an optional `organizationId?: string`. The changeset calls this "not exported by name": literally true (`index.ts` does not list the interface), but it is reachable from the entry type graph through the exported `ApprovalServiceOptions.messaging` and the public `ApprovalService.attachMessaging(…)`, so it is published surface, not shipped bytes. Additive and optional, no consumer rewrites anything: **right as a change; the changeset sentence under-states reachability** — see ②.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body, the claim's line copied verbatim. **Right.** The path limb is clear (no `packages/spec/src/**` file) and the declared limb is honest: no key is added to a published payload — `sys_notification.organization_id` gains VALUES in a column it already had, and the only new key is the optional one on the in-process messaging surface above. The `(narrowing)` arm is right and was measured before it was kept (H5): the accept set of `sys_notification` system writes, of `MessagingService.emit()` and of the `notify` step all shrink where no owner is derivable — BREAKING.
- `.changeset/23284-notification-takes-record-organization.md`: `objectql`, `service-messaging`, `service-automation` at `minor` — **right**; a breaking change ships `minor` under the launch-window convention and `check-changeset-no-major` is green on this head. `plugin-approvals` at `patch` — **wrong by the letter of the level rule**: a purely additive widening of a published package's public surface takes at least `minor` (the rule `check-changeset-no-major` and the `Check Changeset` step state), and the optional `organizationId` on `ApprovalMessagingSurface` is reachable published surface (①-4). The published version is unaffected — the fixed group ships every package at the group's highest bump, `minor` — so this is a declaration error, not a release error. Patch round: grade `plugin-approvals` `minor` and rewrite the "not exported by name" sentence to say the key is reachable through `ApprovalServiceOptions.messaging`.
- Body: the BREAKING banner, the owner rules, the "Refused now" paragraph and the remedy ("give the notification an owner": `sourceObject` + `sourceId`, `organization` on the start node, or `organizationId` to `emit()`) — the text an upgrading agent greps. ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: **right** — nothing authorable is removed, renamed or re-shaped and no stored row is rewritten; the remedy is authoring guidance for a runtime refusal, not a FROM → TO rewrite of a retired spelling; `check:adr-0087-registration` accepted it on this head (Lint & Repo Gates green).
- Checks on the head, read through the API once every run had completed: 40 runs — 32 success, 6 skipped, 2 failure; all six `Test Core` shards, `Build Core`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` green. Two are red, and the same-signature-on-base exception does not apply — the merge base `cc14657ede` has `Type Check · workspace` and `TypeScript Type Check` green (jobs 115516838615 and 115522226805), and the error names a symbol this diff orphaned:
  - `Type Check · workspace` (job 115553650674) — FAIL. Failing step: "Type check workspace packages" (`type-check-workspace-packages`); `pnpm run typecheck` in `packages/services/service-automation` exited 2. First error line: `src/builtin/notify-organization-stamp.integration.test.ts(64,10): error TS6133: 'recordingLogger' is declared but its value is never read.`
  - `TypeScript Type Check` (job 115557073665) — FAIL: the required context, red because the lane above is.
  Cause, read off the diff: the merge base calls `recordingLogger()` once, in the old PIN D; the rewrite of PIN D dropped that call and kept the helper, and the root `tsconfig.json` sets `noUnusedLocals: true`, so `tsc --noEmit` reds on it. The helper is already orphaned at `d564b21d57`, the sha the dev's report cites for "typecheck green for all four packages" — that reading does not hold for `service-automation`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions[0]` — is the ledger admission a maintainer decision? The claim amendment (6155816752) answered A; **this record confirms A**: the ledger header's admission bar is a citable writer fact, the entry cites the maintainer's ruling naming the table verbatim and the writers this diff lands, and only the one object is admitted — `sys_inbox_message` and `sys_notification_receipt` stay unclassified and follow the event row through `emit()`, which keeps a receipt for a legacy NULL notification writable until the v18 ceremony attributes the residue. The right scope; not escalated.
- Deviation 1 (file surface beyond the claim: the objectql ledger and its classification test) — accepted by the claim amendment; the file list touches neither `engine.ts` (#23315) nor `builtin/config-parse*` (#23319). Answered.
- Deviation 2 (the booted measurement harness is not committed) — the committed pins cover each seam on its own: the engine rule on a real `ObjectQL`, family-follows-event on a real `ObjectQL`, the node's anchors with the real engine and messaging service, the approvals battery. Accepted; no committed pin boots `ScheduleTrigger` itself, which deviation 4 covers.
- Deviation 3 (bump levels) — judged in ②: three right, `plugin-approvals` to `minor`.
- Deviation 4 (the schedule tick is hand-built, not a fired job) — verified against `ScheduleTrigger` on `main`: its literal is `event: 'schedule'`, `tenantId` OMITTED for an undeclared flow, `params: { jobId, flowName, schedule }`, `callerParamKeys: []`; the test's `SCHEDULE_TICK` matches it key for key. Answered.
- Deviations 5–8 (model-free commit trailers; the deepened clone and the eight dists built for two gates; an overlapped gate run superseded by the complete one; worktree cleanup) — local acts, nothing in the diff. Answered.
- Out-of-scope (a): an organization-less schedule run on `single` holding two organizations has its own `sys_automation_run` row refused and logged at ERROR, before and after — the ruled loud behaviour (D9; `ScheduleTrigger`'s BIND line predicts it), in `engine.ts` held by #23315. Accepted as noted; no card.
- Out-of-scope (b): HotCRM's `case_sla_monitor` and `task_urgent_alert` declare no `sourceObject` / `sourceId`; on an install holding several organizations the record-less alert is refused until the node names the case. Escalated to the `repo:hotcrm` seat with the landing note by the claim amendment. Answered.
- Dev's `tests` field, "typecheck green for all four packages" — does not hold on this head (② above); the report's other readings (full suites at `d564b21d57`, the two ablations with blob-verified restores, 70 of 70 gate commands) are consistent with the diff and with the green runs.

The diff's semantics pass on every item above. The verdict is FAIL on the required check: `TypeScript Type Check` is red on this head for a cause inside the diff. Patch round: delete the unused `recordingLogger` helper in `notify-organization-stamp.integration.test.ts` (or give it a caller), grade `plugin-approvals` `minor` and correct the changeset's reachability sentence. Nothing else in the diff needs to move; a new record on the new head follows.
